name: Settle with the IESO
summary: Each month the utility settles with the IESO, which runs the Ontario wholesale market: it files a claim by the fourth business day for the difference between what Regulated Price Plan customers paid and what the market charged, with true-ups for earlier months, pays the IESO invoice for energy, global adjustment and other charges within two business days of its issue, and reconciles everything to the regulatory variance accounts. Settlement analysts do the work in spreadsheets fed by the billing system, with a supervisor's review and finance releasing the payment. It is error-prone because the first claim must rest on estimated volumes and prices, and errors only surface in later true-ups or when the OEB tests the variance account balances.

baseline.org_archetype: A municipally owned Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers buying about $1B a year of power through the IESO.
baseline.notes: One case is one month's settlement, from month-end to the variance reconciliation and cash forecast; the February 2019 OEB accounting guidance set the method for the whole period.

trigger: Calendar month-end: the trade month closes and settlement data for it must be prepared.
end_state: The settlement claim is filed, the IESO invoice is paid, journal entries are posted, variance accounts are reconciled and treasury has the next cash forecast.

volume.seasonality: One settlement a month; year-end adds the final true-ups needed for rate application disposition, and July adds Class A and Class B reclassification.

evidence.note: RPP settlement claims are made for each calendar month (ag2019).
Org file has 4 settlement and retailer analysts; about one FTE on IESO settlement, the rest on retailer EBT transactions. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
Two reviews a month. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
Payment and journal entries. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
Releases the IESO wire; not listed for this process in the organisation file's process map. Loaded cost from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).

systems.name: Provincial Meter Data Management/Repository (IESO Smart Metering Entity) portal
Local meter data management and validation tool
ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Electronic business transaction (EBT) hub for retailer transactions
Online IESO settlement and participant reports portal

steps.name: Run month-end billing and consumption extracts
steps.description: After month-end the CIS and reporting tools produce extracts of billed kWh by RPP time-of-use period and tier, non-RPP and retailer kWh, Class A customer volumes, and unbilled days by account for the trade month.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of monthly IESO settlement work at an Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Download IESO statements and wholesale data
steps.description: A settlement analyst downloads the IESO preliminary settlement statements and wholesale meter data for the month's trade days, the posted average energy price and the global adjustment second estimate, and loads them into the settlement workbook.

error.defect_description: A trade day's statement missing from the download.

evidence.note: Preliminary statements are available ten business days after each trade day (iesosettle); the GA second estimate is used for the initial claim (ag2019).

steps.name: Estimate RPP and non-RPP volumes for the month
steps.description: Two analysts estimate the calendar month's loss-adjusted kWh by RPP time-of-use period and tier and for non-RPP customers, using billed data plus interval data for unbilled days, and check that the total matches wholesale purchases apart from losses.

error.defect_description: Volume estimate off, corrected by the later true-ups.

evidence.note: Distributors estimate calendar-month RPP and non-RPP volumes by rate point for the day-4 claim, and RPP plus non-RPP volumes must match wholesale purchases apart from losses (ag2019).

steps.name: Calculate initial RPP settlement claim
steps.description: The analyst calculates the difference between what RPP customers were charged at RPP prices and what the market charged at the average energy price plus the GA second estimate, producing the initial claim for charge type 1142.

error.defect_description: Price point applied to the wrong period.

evidence.note: Initial claim through CT 1142 using RPP prices, estimated average energy price and GA second estimate (ag2019).

steps.name: Calculate first true-up for prior month
steps.description: The analyst reverses last month's initial claim and recalculates it with the actual global adjustment price from last month's IESO invoice and the actual energy price, and records the difference as an adjustment.

error.defect_description: Wrong GA price or Class B volume used.

evidence.note: First true-up replaces the GA second estimate with the actual GA price the month after the initial claim (ag2019).

steps.name: Calculate second true-up with actual volumes
steps.description: For the month two or three months back the analyst replaces estimated volumes with actual billed kWh by price point now that the cycles are billed, and calculates the second true-up.

error.defect_description: Billing corrections after the extract are missed.

evidence.note: Second true-up with actual kWh volumes, known by the second or third month after the trade month (ag2019).

steps.name: Prepare embedded generation settlement
steps.description: The analyst totals the month's kWh and contract payments for FIT and microFIT generators connected to the utility's system from the CIS, checks new and terminated contracts, and prepares the amounts to claim from the IESO.

error.defect_description: A new contract or a changed meter is missed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of monthly IESO settlement work at an Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers, 2019-2022. Ontario distributors settle FIT and microFIT contract payments through the IESO.

steps.name: Compile Class A and Class B global adjustment data
steps.description: The analyst compiles Class A customers' consumption and peak demand factors and the Class B volume so the global adjustment is split correctly, and checks customers who moved between classes on July 1.

error.defect_description: Class A customer volume missing.

evidence.note: Class A customers pay GA based on peak demand factor and Class A volumes reported to the IESO must agree (qa2019).

steps.name: Review and approve settlement submission
steps.description: The billing supervisor checks the workbook: volumes against last month and last year, price points, the true-ups and the embedded generation totals, and either approves the submission or sends questions back.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: settlement claims prepared by one person and reviewed by another

evidence.note: Author's estimate of monthly IESO settlement work at an Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Submit settlement data to the IESO
steps.description: The analyst keys the RPP settlement claim, true-ups and embedded generation amounts into the IESO's online settlement forms by the fourth business day after month-end and saves the confirmation.

error.defect_description: Keying error in the online form.

control.basis: OEB Accounting Procedures Handbook guidance on Accounts 1588 and 1589 and IESO market rules: initial RPP settlement claim filed by business day 4

evidence.note: Claims filed with the IESO by the 4th business day after month-end (ag2019).

steps.name: Wait for the IESO monthly invoice
steps.description: The IESO issues its monthly invoice ten business days after month-end, bundling preliminary, final and recalculated statements since the last invoice, including energy, global adjustment, market charges, transmission and the RPP settlement.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Invoices are published ten business days after the calendar month ends (iesosettle). The page is current; applying the same timetable to 2019-2022 is the author's assumption.

steps.name: Review IESO invoice by charge type
steps.description: The analyst compares each charge type on the invoice (energy, global adjustment, RPP settlement, transmission network and connection, wholesale market service, embedded generation) with the submission and expectations, and checks recalculated statements for earlier months.

error.defect_description: A recalculated prior-month charge is not noticed.

evidence.note: Each invoice bundles preliminary, final and recalculated statements (iesosettle); time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Query or dispute invoice difference
steps.description: For an unexplained difference the analyst traces it to a trade day and charge type, contacts IESO settlements or files a notice of disagreement within the window, and notes the amount for the reconciliation. Payment still goes ahead on time.
outputs: IESO query or notice of disagreement

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Notices of disagreement are filed through Online IESO within six to ten business days of the statement (iesosettle).

steps.name: Prepare IESO payment
steps.description: An accountant prepares the wire for the net invoice amount, tens of millions of dollars, in the banking platform and the ERP, attaching the invoice and the analyst's review, so it settles within two business days of the invoice.

error.defect_description: Wrong amount or date keyed.

control.basis: IESO market rules: participants owing money pay within two business days of the invoice

evidence.note: Participants owing the IESO pay within two business days of receiving the invoice (iesosettle, current page applied to 2019-2022).

steps.name: Approve and release the wire
steps.description: The director of finance checks the amount against the invoice and cash forecast and releases the wire in the banking platform as the second signer.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Treasury policy: dual authorization of large wires

evidence.note: Author's estimate of monthly IESO settlement work at an Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Record cost of power journal entries
steps.description: The accountant records the invoice by charge type in the cost of power accounts (power purchased, global adjustment, transmission, market charges), reverses the estimate accrued at month-end and records the RPP settlement amounts.

error.defect_description: Charge type posted to the wrong account.

evidence.note: Monthly cost of power and RPP settlement entries in Accounts 4705 and 4707 (ag2019).

steps.name: Settle amounts with retailers
steps.description: The analyst reconciles amounts billed to retailer customers with the retailer settlement transactions from the EBT hub and prepares the monthly retailer payments and settlement statements.

error.defect_description: Retailer amount mismatched.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of monthly IESO settlement work at an Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers, 2019-2022. Retailer transactions from the organisation file's cs-retailer-ebt process.

steps.name: Reconcile variance accounts 1588 and 1589
steps.description: The analyst reconciles the month's power and global adjustment revenue and cost, RPP and non-RPP, including the true-ups, to the retail settlement variance accounts 1588 and 1589, explains the movement and updates the GA analysis workform used in rate applications.

error.defect_description: Reconciling item left unexplained.

evidence.note: Timely true-ups keep RPP and non-RPP variances in the correct account for disposition (ag2019).

steps.name: Review variance reconciliation
steps.description: The billing supervisor reviews the reconciliation and unexplained differences and signs it off for month-end close and the regulatory accounts team.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting and OEB review of commodity variance balances at disposition

evidence.note: Author's estimate of monthly IESO settlement work at an Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers, 2019-2022.

steps.name: Update cash forecast for next payment
steps.description: The analyst estimates next month's IESO payment from consumption trends and posted prices and sends it to treasury for the cash and credit facility forecast.

error.defect_description: Forecast misses a GA price swing.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of monthly IESO settlement work at an Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers, 2019-2022.

exceptions.name: Submission sent back
exceptions.description: The supervisor questions the volumes or true-ups and the analysts rework them before the day-4 deadline.

exceptions.name: Invoice difference
exceptions.description: An invoice charge does not match expectations; the analyst queries the IESO or files a notice of disagreement, but pays on time.

exceptions.name: Reconciling items
exceptions.description: The variance reconciliation has unexplained items that must be cleared before sign-off.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month-end to reconciliation signed off
benchmarks.population: Ontario distributors settling with the IESO, 2019-2022

evidence.note: Claim by business day 4 (ag2019), invoice on business day 10 and payment within two business days (iesosettle) put payment at about day 16; reconciliation and sign-off in the following week are the author's estimate.
Current IESO page; applied to 2019-2022 by assumption.

pain_points.description: The day-4 claim rests on estimated volumes and the GA second estimate, so every month needs two true-ups and errors persist for months.

evidence.note: Initial claim on estimates, first and second true-ups (ag2019).

pain_points.description: The settlement runs in linked spreadsheets kept by one or two analysts, so knowledge and checks depend on a few people.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of monthly IESO settlement work at an Ontario distributor of about 350,000 customers, 2019-2022.

pain_points.description: Variance balances in Accounts 1588 and 1589 are tested by the OEB at disposition; settlement errors found then mean restating balances and explaining adjustments in the rate application.

evidence.note: Transitional adjustments must be explained and reconciled at the next rate application (ag2019).

pain_points.description: The IESO payment of tens of millions of dollars falls due two business days after the invoice, which makes cash timing tight.

evidence.note: Two business days to pay (iesosettle); cost of power of about $984M a year from the organisation file.

sources.title: Accounting Procedures Handbook Update: Accounting Guidance related to Commodity Pass-Through Accounts 1588 & 1589
sources.supports: RPP settlement claims for each calendar month through CT 1142 filed by the 4th business day; estimated volumes by RPP rate point; GA second estimate; first and second true-ups; monthly accounting entries; Accounts 1588 and 1589; effective 1 January 2019.

sources.title: Accounts 1588 and 1589 Q&As (accounting guidance questions and answers)
sources.supports: Class A global adjustment based on peak demand factor; Class A volumes reported to the IESO; invoiced GA price used for settlements.

sources.title: Settlement Process (preliminary and final statements, monthly invoices, payment deadlines)
sources.supports: Preliminary statements ten business days after each trade day; monthly invoices ten business days after month-end; payment within two business days; notices of disagreement within six to ten business days. Current IESO page; the timetable is taken to apply to 2019-2022.

assumptions: The organisation file lists the IESO invoice, customer bills and retailer transactions as triggers; the monthly case actually starts at month-end and the invoice arrives mid-case, so the IESO invoice is kept as the trigger for consistency with the organisation file and bills and retailer transactions are standing inputs.
Multi-hour analysis steps are elapsed working time; overnight gaps are written as waits so the day-4 deadline falls about five to six calendar days after month-end.
Embedded generation (FIT and microFIT) settlement and retailer settlement are included because the same analysts do them in the same monthly cycle.
The finance director is added as the wire's second signer, a role the organisation file's process map does not list for this process.

Touch times are the author's estimates. Modelled hands-on time is about 50 hours a month (0.4 FTE); the stated 1.0 FTE also covers work not modelled step by step: IESO queries between cycles, year-end true-ups for rate application disposition, the GA analysis workform and responses to OEB interrogatories on Accounts 1588 and 1589.
